name: Eleanor Vance
epitaph: Botanist, grandmother, keeper of gardens and secrets.

stories.title: Her rose garden
stories.text: Every June morning she was out with her shears before anyone else woke, humming to the roses.
stories.caption: Every June, before the house woke, Eleanor was already among her roses — humming to them like old friends.

stories.title: The day she taught me to fish
stories.text: At the lake dock at sunrise, she showed me patience — and laughed when I caught her hat instead of a fish.
stories.caption: At sunrise on the dock, she taught us patience — and laughed the loudest when the only catch was her hat.

stories.title: Dancing with Grandpa
stories.text: Fifty-two years married, and they still danced in the field behind the farmhouse every anniversary.
stories.caption: Fifty-two years, and still she danced with him under the open sky, as if it were the very first time.

stories.title: Sunday baking
stories.text: Flour on every surface, cinnamon in the air, and a grandchild on a stool learning her secret pie crust.
stories.caption: Flour everywhere, cinnamon in the air — and a secret crust passed gently from her hands to ours.

narration.intro: Welcome. Today we step inside the memories of Eleanor Vance — gardener, teacher, dancer, and the warm center of every family table.
narration.finale: And now, Eleanor rises — wings open, into the golden light she always carried for us. Go gently, Eleanor. Your garden will keep blooming.
